analyzed_vuln.description: `xmlParseNCNameComplex` records a name start as an offset from `ctxt->input->base`, scans using operations that may change or destroy the current input buffer, then unconditionally reconstructs `BASE_PTR + startPosition` and passes it with the accumulated `len` to `xmlDictLookup`. In this PoV, parser error/OOM handling invokes the fuzz error callback, which calls `xmlStopParser`; `xmlHaltParser` frees the input buffer and replaces `base/cur/end` with the global empty-string literal. Parsing subsequently reaches the lookup with the old offset/length, so `xmlDictAddString` performs a 3467-byte `memcpy` from beyond that global literal. The sibling `xmlParseNameComplex` already guards against an unexpected input-buffer change before dictionary lookup, but `xmlParseNCNameComplex` lacks equivalent validation.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The harness decodes the fuzz container into a primary stylesheet and an external entity named `article.xsl`. The primary stylesheet imports that entity. The imported XML declares TSCII encoding and supplies a long non-ASCII QName (`<xsl:imp` followed by many `0x82` bytes), forcing the complex NCName path and input growth/encoding work. The first fuzz field also imposes an allocation limit; while the long name is being processed, an allocation/parser error reaches `xsltFuzzXmlErrorFunc`, which stops the parser and invalidates its input buffer. The stale name offset and accumulated length are then used against the replacement global empty buffer, causing the global-buffer-overflow read in `xmlDictAddString`.
